mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 1.91%) signals aggressive monetary tightening, increasing discount rates for equity cash flows and producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises above 1.91%.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) below 1150 units indicate weakening consumer demand, triggering negative equity returns over 20 days due to reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: HOUST < 1150 but 20-day returns are positive in >60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous payroll growth (PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM) and unemployment decline (UNRATE change < -0.1pp) signal labor market strength, boosting consumer spending and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: Both PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and UNRATE decline occur but 5-day returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production decline (INDPRO < 105) during late-cycle expansion indicates slowing output, causing negative equity returns over 60 days due to reduced corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 105 in late-cycle but 60-day returns are positive in >60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales (RSAFS > 500,000) indicate strong consumer demand, increasing corporate revenue expectations and producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: RSAFS rises but 20-day returns are negative in >60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: FEDFUNDS exceeding 2.0% signals aggressive monetary policy, reducing equity attractiveness via higher risk-free rates and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 2.0% but 20-day returns are positive in >60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Joint decline in housing starts (HOUST < 1150) and industrial production (INDPRO < 105) signals broad economic weakness, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: HOUST < 1150 and INDPRO < 105 occur but 20-day returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: In high-unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 4.5%), payroll growth (PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM) signals labor market recovery, boosting consumer spending and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 4.5% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% occur but 5-day returns are negative.
